newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ government posts improved surplus to April.
newsitem.headline: NZ government posts improved surplus to April.

text.p: The New Zealand government said on Friday it posted a NZ$3.072 billion operating budget surplus for the ten months to April 30, 1997, against a revised forecast surplus of $2.912 billion.
Net public debt as a percentage of GDP was 27.0 percent at April 30 against a forecast 27.1 percent, and compared with 29.1 percent at December 31 and 31.5 percent at June 30, 1996.
Tax revenue was up 0.5 percent on forecast at $29.895 billion.

Treasury in its Current-year Fiscal Update (CFU) on May 21 revised its forecast for the 1996/97 year to NZ$2.312 billion from NZ$2.493 billion in the previous forecast in the December Econonomic and Fiscal Update (DEFU).
Treasury said in Friday's news release that the operating balance was $160 million ahead of forecast largely due to higher than forecast goods and services tax and source deductions revenue.
Net public debt was $25.038 billion, $41 million (0.2 percent) lower than forecast and $3.599 billion (12.6 percent) lower than at June 1996.
The government's net worth was estimated at April 30 at $6.651 billion, $161 million higher than forecast thanks to a higher operating balance and net asset revaluations of $235 million.
The financial statements for the 11 months to May 31 will be released with the Budget on June 26.
